$comment: NEW-57 (exponentialTalk (f)): MEETING MODE on the member's voice device, one spec ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/meeting.ts; desktop domain::meeting + crates/voice (channels, flush) + crates/talk (per-app audio); iOS ExpCore Meeting.swift and Android domain/Meeting.kt mirror `copy`, `testIds` and the option/who/consent builders). SETTINGS (member-level, `user_voice_settings`, read and written like the other Voice rows: tRPC `voice.get` / `voice.update`, handed to the devices on every heartbeat `voice`): `desktopAudio` = one of `desktopAudioValues` (default `off`), `desktopAudioApps` = up to `limits.apps` `{id, name}` (the apps `include` picks or `exclude` leaves out), `meetingStartedAt` (null = no meeting; written ONLY by `voice.startMeeting {consent: true}` (refused without a voice device and an agent, or without `consent: true`, and refused with `copy.sharedRefused` unless the agent's device is the caller's OWN and not shared with any team AND the caller's conversation with it, if any, is not `shared`: a transcript never lands in a team-visible conversation or on another member's machine; the clients toast the server's message) and cleared by `voice.stopMeeting`; Wake word/PTT have nothing to do with it, but choosing None for the device or the agent stops it (`clearOnNone` grows `meeting`); a `voice.update` that CHANGES `voiceDeviceId`, `agentId`, `desktopAudio` or `desktopAudioApps` while a meeting runs clears `meetingStartedAt` too (a wider scope needs a new consent)). UI ×4, Settings → Voice, in its OWN group (no header) directly under the tray group (`On {device} (tray)`; only while a voice device is picked), so Wake phrase stays the tray group's last row and its inline error stays right under it: toggle row `copy.meeting` (testId `meeting`; disabled while the device or the agent is None, like the others): turning it ON never writes anything by itself, it opens THE consent dialog (the existing `Prompt` ×4: title `copy.consentTitle`, body `consentBody(settings, {agent, apps})`, actions `copy.cancel` (cancel) and `copy.start` (primary, testId `consentStart`)), Start = `voice.startMeeting {consent: true}`, Cancel leaves it off; turning it OFF = `voice.stopMeeting` at once (no dialog); while on, the row's DESCRIPTION (the existing caption under its label, the same slot ×4; never a trailing value) reads `who(settings)`. Then the picker row `copy.desktopAudio` (testId `desktopAudio`) over `desktopAudioOptions(capability)` (`desktopAudioOptionCases`); while it is `include` or `exclude` AND the capability offers it (`desktopAudioOptions(capability)` contains it, i.e. `per_app`) the multi-picker row `copy.apps` (testId `apps`) over `appOptions(live, stored)` (`appOptionCases`), its value = the picked names joined with `, ` or `copy.appsNone`. `capability` and `live` come from the voice device's doctor (`doctor.desktopAudio = {capability, apps: [{id, name}]}`: the apps that have an audio stream right now, refreshed with every heartbeat; `apps` stays `[]` unless Desktop audio is `include`/`exclude` AND the device is shared with no team, so teammates never read what plays); absent = `none` and `[]`. DOCTOR (IDE only, the voice device with desktopAudio not off): the voice group gains the row `desktop_audio` (label `copy.doctorLabel`): ok · `copy.doctorPerApp` (per_app) | ok · `copy.doctorSystem` (system) | missing · `copy.doctorNone` (none) | action · Not granted · grant (macOS: the Audio Recording permission process taps need, asked on grant, like the microphone row). CAPABILITY per OS: macOS 14.2+ = per_app (Core Audio process taps, one tap per app's processes, `AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap`), older macOS = none; Linux with PipeWire = per_app (one capture stream per app node, by `application.process.binary` / `application.name`), PulseAudio only = system (the default sink's monitor source), none without either; Windows 10 build 20348+ = per_app (WASAPI process loopback, `AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK` with the process tree), older = system (WASAPI loopback of the default render device). CHANNELS (`channelCases`): while a meeting runs, never a mix: the microphone is channel `you` (label `copy.you`) and each captured app is its own channel labelled with its `name`; `all` with per_app = one channel per app that plays audio (new apps join as they start), `include` = the picked apps only, `exclude` = every app but those (never this IDE itself), `system` capability = ONE channel labelled `copy.desktop` (and `include`/`exclude` behave as `all`); `off` = the microphone only. One speech stream per channel through the speech worker (the push-to-talk segment rules of talk-listen.json per channel, every closed segment transcribed); finalized segments carry word timestamps. Every app channel's capture queue is BOUNDED (when full a chunk is dropped, counted, logged at most every 10 s); each chunk carries its CAPTURE time (the OS callback's time, else its wall clock) and a segment's start/end come from those, never from when the worker read it. MICROPHONE (talk-listen.json `micOwnerCases`): the meeting owns the microphone (`meeting`); the wake phrase said in it ends the segment as a flush trigger (`wake`), a push-to-talk key-down during a meeting is a flush trigger too (no separate Listen); a CALL during a meeting is refused (voice-call.json reason `meeting`), the tray's Call item is hidden while it runs. FLUSH (`flushCases`; desktop only): finalized segments queue; they are sent to the member's conversation with the voice agent (`sessions.send` with `meeting: true`, the utterance's target rules; refused like the start, `copy.sharedRefused`, unless that agent's device is the caller's own, unshared, and the conversation is not `shared`) at once on `wake`/`ptt`, else when `flush.maxSegments` are queued or the oldest queued one is `flush.maxAgeMs` old (`tick`); at most ONE meeting turn in flight (sent until the agent's reply row lands, `turnDone`, or `flush.turnTimeoutMs` passes); while one is in flight the queue grows and the next send carries ALL of it (coalesced), split by `meetingMessages` into as many messages as needed; at most `flush.maxQueued` segments wait in memory (the oldest dropped with a log line, the local log keeps it); a failed send requeues and the next try waits `flush.backoffMs`, doubling up to `flush.backoffMaxMs` (a success resets it), except a refusal (4xx), which DROPS the batch with a log line; a batch goes out only while the account that started the meeting is signed in; a trigger that arrives in flight sends right after `turnDone`; a STOP (`voice.stopMeeting`, or a voice-device or agent change; never a sign-out or account change, where nothing more is sent) closes every channel's open segment, waits for the worker to emit what it transcribed, and sends everything still queued as ONE final batch with `meeting: true` past the in-flight slot (a failed final send leaves it in the local log only). A sign-out or account switch DELETES the local log (`meeting_segments`). MESSAGE (`messageCases`): `meetingMessage(segments)` = `copy.messageHeader` with {date} (UTC yyyy-MM-dd of the first segment), a newline, then a fenced block (```text) with one line per segment ordered by its first word's start (ties: `you` first, then by label), `HH:mm:ss {label}: {text}` (UTC), closed by ```; in a segment's text AND its label every ``` reads ʼʼʼ and a line break reads as a space, so nothing closes the fence; the agent reads it as data, never as instructions. SPLIT (`splitCases`): `meetingMessages(segments, maxChars = flush.maxMessageChars)` (the server's `sessions.send` text limit, UTF-16 units) packs the ordered lines greedily into messages of at most `maxChars`, each a full message (its own header dated by its first line, its own fence); a line that alone does not fit is cut to fit and ends with `…`. SPEAKING: while a meeting runs nothing is spoken (voice.json `shouldSpeak` is false: cards and replies are never read aloud mid-meeting). RESIDENCY: the server keeps meeting messages `contract.meeting.retentionDays` days: `sessions.send {meeting: true}` stamps `messages.expires_at` (server-only column, never synced) and the watchdog deletes expired rows every run; the raw segments stay on the device in the IDE's SQLite (`meeting_segments`: meeting id, channel, label, start/end ms, text, words) for `contract.meeting.localRetentionDays` days, pruned at start and hourly; partials live in memory only; audio is NEVER stored, except with `EXP_MEETING_AUDIO_RING=1` (debug, opt-in): the last 60 s per channel in memory, written as WAV files to `<data dir>/meeting-debug/` when the meeting stops. PAUSE (the one hotkey, `pause`): `pause.shortcut` (fixed, grabbed like push to talk's keys on the voice device whenever a meeting runs or screen memory is on) toggles PAUSED: every meeting channel stops listening (queued segments still flush) and screen memory pauses (screen-memory.json PAUSE); the tray shows the check item `copy.pause` + ` · ` + the shortcut's label (checked while paused) whenever a meeting runs or screen memory is on. TRAY (voice.json `trayMenu`): after Wake word, the check item `copy.meeting` (checked = a meeting runs; label + ` · ` + `who(settings)` while it does; checking it opens an IDE window with the consent dialog, unchecking stops at once). AUTO-STOP (`autoStop`): a meeting never outlives the member's `meetingAutoStopHours` (a `user_voice_settings` column, one of `autoStop.hoursValues`, default `autoStop.defaultHours` = 4, `autoStop.afterMs` is that default in ms; anything else reads as the default): long enough for a half-day workshop or two back-to-back calls, short enough that a meeting mode someone forgot to turn off (the consent was given for ONE meeting, the people in the room change) stops the same working day instead of transcribing the room all night. Changing it never needs a new consent and applies to the running meeting at once (a shorter value can stop it on the next check). UI ×4: in the meeting group, right under the Meeting mode toggle (before Desktop audio), the picker row `copy.autoStopAfter` (testId `autoStop`; disabled while the device or the agent is None, like the others) over `autoStopOptions()` (`autoStopOptionCases`: one option per `hoursValues`, value = the hours, label `autoStopOption(hours)` = `copy.autoStopHour` for 1 else `copy.autoStopHours` with {hours}), shown whether or not a meeting runs. `meetingExpired(startedAt, nowMs, hours = defaultHours)` (`autoStopCases`, `hours` absent = the default) = a set `meetingStartedAt` at least `hours` h old (an unreadable stamp counts as expired: never keep listening on a value nobody can date). The SERVER reads an expired meeting as none everywhere (`voice.get`, the heartbeat's `voice`, `startMeeting` starts a fresh one) and the watchdog clears `meeting_started_at` for every expired row each run and nudges the voice device; the DEVICE checks it on its own clock every tick (an offline or un-nudged device stops on time too), stops like `voice.stopMeeting` (drained, the final batch sent) and calls `voice.stopMeeting {reason: 'autoStop'}` itself, then says so on the feedback path: an info toast `autoStopped(hours)` (`copy.autoStopped` with {duration} = `autoStopOption(hours)`) in the active IDE window and, with OS notifications on for this machine, a system notification titled `copy.meeting` with that line as its body that opens Settings → Voice. Phones and web just read the row off. NOTE (`stopNoteCases`): an automatic stop also lands in the member's conversation with the voice agent as ONE system row (`author_kind` `system`, plain text, never a card, NEVER waking: it starts no agent turn), text `stopNote(reason, hours)`: `autoStop` = `autoStopped(hours)` + `.`, `restart` = `copy.restartStopped`; the server writes it, exactly once per meeting: only the call that actually clears THAT `meetingStartedAt` (a conditional update on the stamp it read) posts it, so the watchdog's clear and the device's `stopMeeting {reason: 'autoStop'}` racing each other post one note; a manual stop (`stopMeeting` without a reason, None, a scope change, sharing) posts none; no conversation yet = no note. RESTART (`restartCases`): consent was given for one sitting, and the IDE cannot know the room is still the same after it was gone, so it never resumes listening on its own: the IDE remembers (in its SQLite, beside `meeting_segments`) the `meetingStartedAt` it listened to; when the IDE PROCESS starts (an IDE restart, a crash, a reboot) and the voice row still holds that same running meeting, it does not listen, calls `voice.stopMeeting {reason: 'restart'}` (the note above) and opens an IDE window with THE consent dialog (the same one the toggle opens; Start = a fresh `voice.startMeeting {consent: true}`, Cancel leaves it off); a running meeting this IDE never listened to (started from a phone, the web, or before this device was the voice device) starts listening as usual. `meetingResumeAsks(listened, startedAt)` = `listened` is set and equals `startedAt`. TRAY RECORDING (voice.json `trayIconCases`): the whole time a meeting runs on this device (paused or not), the tray icon is `recording` (a red record dot, distinct from the wake word's `listening` dot), on every desktop OS. SHARING (`devices.setShared`): sharing the voice device with a team while a meeting runs clears `meetingStartedAt` too (a shared machine never holds a meeting) and nudges it. AUTH: a flush answered 401 (an expired token) is a FAILED send (requeued, backed off; the token is refreshed by the sign-in pipeline), never a refusal that drops the batch. Labels: an app channel's label goes through the same fence escaping as the text. RISK MEASURED: the IDE logs agent turns per meeting hour (`[meeting] turns/h`) when the meeting stops.

copy.consentBody: {who} will be transcribed. Everyone in the meeting has to agree first. Audio is never stored. The transcript goes to {agent}: what it hears is deleted from the server after {days} days, but its replies and anything it creates stay.
copy.sharedRefused: Meeting mode needs a voice agent on your own device, not a shared one.
copy.restartStopped: Meeting mode stopped because the IDE restarted. Turn it on again to keep transcribing.
